signals.title: AUD/CHF — G10 Bilateral Theme + Hawkish RBA
signals.text: AUD/USD trades at 0.7167, well above its SMA20/50/200 cluster following the release of hawkish RBA minutes and accelerating services inflation in Japan which bolsters the APAC-linked bid. The G10 Currency Strength Scorecard confirms a dominant bilateral theme with AUD outperforming peers by +0.782% while CHF lags at -0.393%, creating a 1.175% spread. This strength is supported by a +435bp AUD/CHF carry premium, though the pair faces a massive retail hurdle with 86% of retail traders currently short. Speculative positioning remains bullish with AUD LF net long at +49,749 (pctl 81), suggesting institutional support for the carry-driven trend. The combination of hawkish central bank rhetoric and a significant carry advantage keeps the pair biased higher despite retail fading. Trade bias: Long AUD/CHF; carry-driven outperformance supported by RBA hawkishness. Catalyst: Australia CPI release Wednesday. Risk: Surprise inflation miss leads to a rapid unwind of the AUD carry premium.

signals.title: USD/CAD — Trade Escalation + ESI Divergence
signals.text: USD/CAD trades at 1.3840, oscillating around its SMA200 of 1.3841 as trade tensions between the US and Canada escalate following retaliatory tariffs. The pair faces a +150bp carry advantage favoring the USD, yet the Economic Surprise Index (ESI) shows a stark divergence with Canada data outperforming (+23.4) while US data disappoints (-12.2). COT positioning for CAD is at a 52-week extreme short with LF net at -89,836 (pctl 13, z -1.48), creating an asymmetric risk for a short-squeeze if trade headlines stabilize. Despite the USD carry advantage, the technical position below the SMA20/50 cluster suggests bearish momentum is building. The dollar is currently caught between trade-driven safe-haven demand and weakening domestic macro data. Trade bias: Bearish USD/CAD; short-squeeze risk on extreme CAD positioning and superior ESI. Catalyst: BoC meeting 9 Sep — hold priced. Risk: Further US trade escalation drives safe-haven flows back into USD, overriding the macro data gap.

signals.title: GBP/USD — Volatility Premium + SMA Support
signals.text: GBP/USD at 1.3648 is holding above its SMA20/50/200 cluster, specifically the SMA20 at 1.3520 which serves as the immediate technical floor. GBP maintains a narrow +8bp carry advantage over the USD according to OIS benchmarks, but the options market is pricing in significant tail risk with an IV of 11.0% against an HV30 of 5.8%. This +5.2% Vol Risk Premium (VRP) is the highest in the G10 space, indicating heavy institutional hedging despite relatively flat speculative positioning (LF net +46,070, pctl 94 but WoW adds slowing). The real rate differential remains supportive for the Pound as the UK real rate of +0.85% exceeds the Eurozone's +0.07%. Markets appear to be paying for protection against a break of the current bullish trend. Trade bias: Neutral GBP/USD; elevated volatility premium suggests caution despite bullish technical alignment. Catalyst: next BoE meeting (mkt: 100% hold priced) 17 Sep. Risk: VRP collapses as realized volatility catches up, forcing a repricing of the directional bias.
